name: Musée des Cultures Contemporaines Adama Toungara (MuCAT)
known: Director General in December 2022: Nathalie Varley Meplon. 60 per cent of visitors come from Abobo, she stated (Djasso, Ethmane Issa, 21 December 2022).
Construction: Director Nathalie Varley Meplon stated the building was constructed "sur fonds propres", from own funds (Djasso, 21 December 2022).

name: Kin ArtStudio
known: The Pro Helvetia interview (12 November 2024) writes the name both as Kin ArtStudio and as KinArt Studios, and names Vitshois Mwilambwe Bondo as its founder.
TEXAF describes Kin ArtStudio as a collective of artists housed in the TEXAF concession in Kinshasa and shows its "Young Congo" exhibition of 11 artists curated by Bondo (TEXAF news item, in Dutch).
Works in partnership with the Montresso Art Foundation, according to its founder Vitshois Mwilambwe Bondo.
Kin ArtStudio's biennale site shows 28 unnamed partner logos with no date; it lists curators and advisers.

name: Texaf Bilembo
known: Former Texaf chief executive Philippe Croonenberghs gave the site to the project (stated by the centre).
Texaf says it is founder and head sponsor of the centre (texaf.be).
Chairman is Dominique Moorkens since May 2023;
Jean-Philippe Waterschoot is chief executive since May 2017 (MarketScreener).

Partners listed on the centre's "Qui sommes-nous" page: TMB, Bracongo, Afrissur, SFA, CFAO, Global Broadband Solution, Canalbox, the Belgian Embassy, the European Union, the Académie des beaux-arts de Kinshasa, IMNC, Enabel, Weyrich Africa, Angalia gallery, the Africa Museum, Louvain Coopération and
Angalia gallery is a listed partner; its news page presents "Papiers de société" (16 April to 30 May 2021, curated by Chantal Tombu) as an exhibition held at the centre.

name: Picha / Lubumbashi Biennale
known: The Art Newspaper reports that Picha was historically self-funded by its founders, with support from private individuals and international bodies including French and Belgian cultural agencies, and that it has no state funding.
Shows the 2026 Biennale sponsors as a page of logos and lists its curators and staff.

name: Kunsten Museum of Modern Art Aalborg
known: Governance: a six-person board chaired by Christen Obel, appointed by the Utzon Foundation.
The Utzon Foundation appoints the chair of Kunsten's board.

name: ARoS
known: Director Rebecca Matthews, board chair Laura Hay Uggla (2025 annual report).
Board members include Marianne Bedsted, a director at Salling, and Helle Østergaard Kristiansen, a senior vice president at Equinor (2025 annual report).

name: Copenhagen Contemporary
known: He was vice-chairman of the board until 2024, and the board was established on 2 December 2014 (Copenhagen Contemporary).

name: Den Frie Centre of Contemporary Art (Den Frie Udstillingsbygning)
known: Its founders included J.F.
A separate building board of a chair and four members serves four-year terms and is appointed in rotation by Den Frie, Akademirådet, AICA and BKF/UKK.
Milena Bonifacini, a visual artist appointed by Den Frie Udstilling, is chair (stated by the space).

name: Designmuseum Danmark
known: Anne-Louise Sommer is director and Henrik Tvarnø chairs the board.

name: Kunsthal Charlottenborg
known: Director: Helene Nyborg Bay.

name: Ny Carlsberg Glyptotek
known: Origin of the money: the brewer Carl Jacobsen founded the Ny Carlsberg Foundation in 1902 and transferred his brewery to the Carlsberg Foundation, founded by his father J.C.

name: O—Overgaden Institut for Samtidskunst
known: Rhea Dall is Director and Chief Curator.
Sanne Kofod Olsen, Vice-Chancellor at the Royal Institute of Art in Stockholm, chairs the board for January 2024 to December 2028.
Board members include Rasmus Myrup, Lea Porsager, Jeannette Ehlers and Rolf Hay, CEO and founder of HAY (Overgaden website).

name: HEART Herning
known: The current board is Lars Damgaard (chair), Johs.
Poulsen (deputy chair), Niels Viggo Malle, Mette Bock, Dann Karlsen and Michael Bjørn Nellemann (stated by the space).

name: Louisiana Museum of Modern Art
known: Poul Erik Tøjner has been director since 2000 (Wikipedia).

name: Trapholt
known: Furniture collection of more than 500 chairs from the 20th century, the largest in Denmark.

Wikipedia reports that in 2000 Marco Evaristti's installation "Helena", blenders holding live goldfish, led to the museum's director being fined for animal cruelty after refusing a police request to turn the blenders off.
